discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and their quantized edge transport (quantum spin Hall and quantum anomalous Hall effects)

nominees.name: Qi-Kun Xue
nominees.affiliation: Southern University of Science and Technology and Tsinghua University, China

subfield: Condensed matter physics (topological phases and quantum transport)
motivation: Kane (with Mele, 2005) showed that spin-orbit coupling can produce a new time-reversal-invariant topological phase, classified by a Z2 invariant, with protected helical edge states. Molenkamp's group first observed this quantum spin Hall state in 2007: HgTe/CdTe quantum wells showed quantized edge conductance of about 2e^2/h. Xue's group achieved the long-sought quantum anomalous Hall effect in 2013: magnetic topological-insulator films showed quantized Hall resistance h/e^2 without any external magnetic field. Together these works established topological insulators, extending the topological ideas behind the quantum Hall effect to a new, broad class of materials. They showed that quantized, dissipationless transport survives in real, disordered materials. This opened the fields of topological materials, Majorana platforms and topological electronics, which now involve thousands of groups worldwide. The link between the topological invariant and the precisely measured transport is exemplary, and Laughlin, Thouless and Haldane's earlier prizes left it unrecognized.
